questions.stem: Pele played for the
explanation_steps: Pelé (Edson Arantes do Nascimento, 1940–2022) played for Brazil (and the club Santos) and won the World Cup three times (1958, 1962, 1970).
He never played for Italy, Spain, the UK or France. Answer: C.
tips: Link famous sports stars with their countries: Pelé – Brazil, Maradona – Argentina, Eusébio – Portugal, George Weah – Liberia.

similar_questions.stem: Diego Maradona, captain of the 1986 World Cup winners, played for which national team?
explanation_steps: Maradona captained Argentina to the 1986 World Cup title in Mexico. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Pelé

questions.stem: ‘Going around the bush’ means:
explanation_steps: The idiom (usually ‘beating about/around the bush’) means avoiding the main topic and talking indirectly instead of saying something clearly.
So it means not coming to the point. Answer: E.
tips: Idioms are never literal: options about forests or President Bush are traps.

similar_questions.stem: ‘Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened!’ The speaker wants the listener to
explanation_steps: The speaker wants the listener to stop avoiding the point and speak directly. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Cambridge Dictionary – ‘beat around the bush’

questions.stem: The current president of France is
explanation_steps: Emmanuel Macron became President of France in May 2017 (re-elected in 2022).
Tony Blair and David Cameron were British prime ministers; Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump are American politicians. Answer: C.
tips: Eliminate by nationality first: only one option is French.

similar_questions.stem: In 2019, who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after Theresa May?
explanation_steps: Boris Johnson succeeded Theresa May in July 2019. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Emmanuel Macron
textbook_ref.note: Time-sensitive: correct in 2019; Macron was re-elected in 2022 and his second term ends in 2027.

questions.stem: Which of the following African countries experienced genocide in the early 1990's?
explanation_steps: In 1994 about 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, were killed in about 100 days in Rwanda – the Rwandan genocide, recognised by the UN (ICTR).
Burundi also suffered massacres (1993), but the event universally called ‘the genocide’ of the early 1990s is Rwanda's. Answer: C.
tips: Rwanda genocide: April–July 1994; remembered each year on 7 April.

similar_questions.stem: The International Criminal Tribunal set up by the UN in Arusha, Tanzania, tried people accused of genocide in
explanation_steps: The ICTR (1994–2015) in Arusha tried those responsible for the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Rwanda genocide of 1994; UN Outreach Programme on the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda
textbook_ref.note: A 1996 UN commission also described the 1993 killings of Tutsi in Burundi as acts of genocide; Rwanda remains the clear answer.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, which ethnic group is dominantly found in Southern Red Sea zone?
explanation_steps: The Afar live in the Danakil lowlands along the southern Red Sea coast (Southern Red Sea zone, Assab, Beilul, Edi) and in neighbouring Ethiopia and Djibouti.
Kunama live in Gash-Barka, Tigrigna in the highlands, Tigre in the north and west, Saho in the eastern escarpment (Northern Red Sea / Debub). Answer: D.
tips: Map the nine ethnic groups to zones: Afar – Southern Red Sea; Kunama and Nara – Gash-Barka; Bilen – Anseba (Keren); Rashaida – northern coast.

similar_questions.stem: The Bilen ethnic group lives mainly around which town?
explanation_steps: The Bilen live mainly in and around Keren, Anseba zone. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Eritrea's nine ethnic groups; Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Afar

questions.stem: Which of the following Eritrean nationalists resisted Italian occupation of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Degiat Bahta Hagos led the 1894 revolt in Akele Guzay and died at the Battle of Halai.

Degiat Aberra Hailu fought the Italians (guerrilla war, battle of Walta Medhanit, Adwa); Mohammed Nuri, a Saho leader, escaped from Nakura prison and attacked the Italians from Tigray together with Ghebremedhin, son of Bahta Hagos.
All the named men are remembered as resisters of Italian colonialism. Answer: E.
tips: When several names in a history item all belong to the same movement, ‘All of the above’ is likely – but only if you can place each one.

similar_questions.stem: The 1894 revolt of Bahta Hagos against the Italians ended at the Battle of
explanation_steps: Bahta Hagos was killed at Halai in December 1894. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – ‘Italian Colonization’ (resistance of Bahta Hagos, Aberra Hailu, Mohammed Nuri, Ghebremedhin)

questions.review_flag: The paper prints ‘Ghebremedhin Hagos’; the resister in the sources is Ghebremedhin (Bahta), son of Bahta Hagos. Keyed E (all).

questions.stem: The Joint Declaration for Peace and Friendship between Eritrea and Ethiopia was signed in Asmara in
explanation_steps: President Isaias Afwerki and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed signed the Joint Declaration of Peace and Friendship in Asmara on 9 July 2018.
A further peace agreement was signed in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on 16 September 2018 – do not confuse the two. Answer: C.
tips: Asmara – July 2018 (Joint Declaration); Jeddah – September 2018 (Agreement on Peace, Friendship and Comprehensive Cooperation).

similar_questions.stem: Where was the September 2018 Eritrea–Ethiopia peace agreement signed?
explanation_steps: The 16 September 2018 agreement was signed in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Joint Declaration of Peace and Friendship between Eritrea and Ethiopia, 9 July 2018

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is associated with Australia?
explanation_steps: Kangaroos are marsupials found naturally only in Australia (and New Guinea); the kangaroo is on Australia's coat of arms.
Zebras, hyenas and ostriches are African; tigers are Asian. Answer: C.
tips: Australia's typical animals are marsupials (kangaroo, koala) and the emu – not the ostrich.

similar_questions.stem: Which animal is Australian rather than African?
explanation_steps: The koala is an Australian marsupial. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Kangaroo

questions.stem: The word democracy comes from the
explanation_steps: ‘Democracy’ comes from Greek dēmos (people) + kratos (power/rule): rule by the people; it began in ancient Athens.
Answer: E.
tips: Many political words are Greek (democracy, monarchy, aristocracy); ‘republic’ is Latin (res publica).

similar_questions.stem: The word ‘republic’ comes from the language of the
explanation_steps: ‘Republic’ is from Latin res publica, ‘the public thing’ – the Romans. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Democracy (etymology)

questions.stem: Insects that can transmit diseases to humans are referred to as
explanation_steps: A vector is a living organism, usually an insect, that carries a pathogen from one host to another (e.g. Anopheles mosquito – malaria).
A carrier is an infected person/animal without symptoms; a reservoir is where the pathogen normally lives. Answer: C.
tips: Mosquitoes, tsetse flies, fleas and sandflies are classic vectors.

similar_questions.stem: The female Anopheles mosquito is the ______ of malaria.
explanation_steps: It carries the Plasmodium parasite between people – a vector. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Vector-borne diseases fact sheet

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important and the first means of mass communication in the world?
explanation_steps: Mass communication began with printing: movable-type printing (Gutenberg, c. 1450) made books and newspapers the first mass media.
Cinema (1890s), radio (1920s), television (1930s–50s) and the internet (1990s) came much later. Answer: A.
tips: Put media in time order: printing → newspapers → cinema → radio → television → internet.

similar_questions.stem: Johannes Gutenberg is famous for introducing
explanation_steps: Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing in Europe around 1450. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Mass media; Printing (Gutenberg)

questions.review_flag: ‘Most important’ is a matter of opinion (radio or the internet could be argued today); keyed A because printing is certainly the first mass medium.

questions.stem: The largest ocean in the world is
explanation_steps: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million km² – about a third of Earth's surface, larger than all land together.
Order: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic. Answer: A.
tips: The Arctic is the smallest ocean.

similar_questions.stem: Which is the smallest of the world's oceans?
explanation_steps: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest (about 14 million km²). Answer: D.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Pacific Ocean

questions.stem: The African country that is <u>not</u> highly dependent on tourist income is
explanation_steps: Kenya and Tanzania (safaris, Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar), Egypt (pyramids, Red Sea resorts) and Rwanda (gorilla trekking) earn a large share of foreign exchange from tourism.
Djibouti's economy rests on its port, logistics and foreign military bases, with little tourism. Answer: A.
tips: Ask what each country is famous for: wildlife and monuments → tourism; ports and transit trade → Djibouti.

similar_questions.stem: Djibouti's economy depends mainly on
explanation_steps: Djibouti earns mostly from its port (Ethiopia's main outlet), logistics and base rents. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: World Bank – Djibouti overview; World Travel & Tourism Council country data

questions.stem: Hypertension is the term used for
explanation_steps: Hypertension = persistently high blood pressure (about 140/90 mmHg or more).
Low blood pressure is hypotension; a fast heart rate is tachycardia and a slow one bradycardia. Answer: A.
tips: hyper- = over/above, hypo- = under/below.

similar_questions.stem: Hypoglycaemia means
explanation_steps: hypo- (low) + glyc (sugar) + -aemia (blood) = low blood sugar. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Hypertension fact sheet

questions.stem: All of the following are <u>not</u> legally accepted in Eritrea <u>except</u>:
explanation_steps: Eritrean law bans FGM (Proclamation 158/2007), child labour, underage marriage (legal age 18) and gender discrimination at work (Labour Proclamation 118/2001).
Private property (houses, businesses, movable goods) is legally recognised – only land belongs to the State. Answer: B.
tips: ‘All are not … except’ = find the one that IS allowed.

similar_questions.stem: In Eritrea, female genital mutilation was banned by law in
explanation_steps: Proclamation No. 158/2007 abolished FGM. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Proclamation No. 158/2007 (abolition of FGM); Labour Proclamation No. 118/2001; Civil Code of Eritrea

questions.stem: The sanction that was imposed on Eritrea by the UN was lifted on
explanation_steps: UN Security Council Resolution 2444 of 14 November 2018 lifted the arms embargo, travel bans, asset freezes and targeted sanctions imposed on Eritrea in 2009.
Answer: A.
tips: Link events of 2018: July – peace declaration; September – Jeddah agreement; November – sanctions lifted.

similar_questions.stem: UN sanctions on Eritrea were first imposed in 2009 by Security Council resolution
explanation_steps: Resolution 1907 (December 2009) imposed them; Resolution 2444 (November 2018) lifted them. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: UN Security Council Resolution 2444 (14 November 2018), press release SC/13576

questions.stem: There are only 2 numbers that are twice the sum of their individual digits, one of them is zero (0). What is the other one?
explanation_steps: Let the number be 10a + b. Condition: 10a + b = 2(a + b) → 8a = b.
With digits 0–9 the only solution besides 0 is a = 1, b = 8 → 18. Check: 1 + 8 = 9 and 2 × 9 = 18. Answer: A.
tips: Test options quickly: 27 → 2 × 9 = 18 ≠ 27; 45 → 18; 40 → 8; 49 → 26. Only 18 works.

similar_questions.stem: Which two-digit number is three times the sum of its digits?

textbook_ref.reference: Elementary algebra (digit problems)

questions.stem: If Ato Abel is the father-in-law of Ato Habte, then Ato Habte’s relation to Ato Abel is
explanation_steps: Abel is Habte's father-in-law, so Habte is married to Abel's daughter.
A man married to someone's daughter is that person's son-in-law (Habte is male – ‘Ato’). Answer: A.
tips: Reverse the relation and keep the gender: father-in-law ↔ son-in-law or daughter-in-law.

similar_questions.stem: W/ro Senait is the mother-in-law of W/ro Luwam. What is Luwam to Senait?
explanation_steps: Luwam is married to Senait's son, so she is Senait's daughter-in-law. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Learner's Dictionary – son-in-law, father-in-law

questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there from 2 to 30?
explanation_steps: 10 is not among the options. If ‘from 2 to 30’ is read as strictly between 2 and 30 (2 excluded), there are 9: 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29.
The intended answer is therefore B (nine), but strictly the correct count, 10, is missing.
tips: Memorise the primes below 30 – there are ten of them; 1 is not prime and 2 is the only even prime.

similar_questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 30 and 50?
explanation_steps: 31, 37, 41, 43, 47 → 5 primes. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Elementary number theory (list of primes)

questions.review_flag: No correct option: there are 10 primes from 2 to 30 inclusive. Keyed B (9) only if 2 is excluded (‘between 2 and 30’). Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is a mammal?
explanation_steps: Mammals have hair and feed their young with milk. The bat is the only flying mammal.
Snake and crocodile are reptiles, ostrich is a bird, amoeba is a single-celled protist. Answer: A.
tips: Flying does not make an animal a bird – bats are mammals; swimming does not make it a fish – whales are mammals.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a mammal?
explanation_steps: The dolphin breathes air and suckles its young – a mammal. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Mammal; Bat

questions.stem: As Asmara is to Eritrea, Dakar is to
explanation_steps: Relation: capital city → country. Asmara is the capital of Eritrea; Dakar is the capital of Senegal.
Lusaka – Zambia, Harare – Zimbabwe, Maputo – Mozambique, Antananarivo – Madagascar. Answer: D.
tips: Find the relation in the first pair (capital → country) and apply it to the second.

similar_questions.stem: As Nairobi is to Kenya, Kampala is to
explanation_steps: Kampala is the capital of Uganda. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Dakar

questions.stem: Which of the following countries share a border with Lake Victoria?
explanation_steps: Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, is shared by Tanzania (about 49%), Uganda (45%) and Kenya (6%).
Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and Ethiopia do not touch it. Answer: D.
tips: Lake Victoria = the three East African Community founders: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania.

similar_questions.stem: Lake Tanganyika is shared by Tanzania, the DR Congo, Zambia and
explanation_steps: Lake Tanganyika borders Tanzania, DR Congo, Burundi and Zambia. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Lake Victoria

questions.stem: Ozone hole refers to

options.B: decrease in the ozone layer in the troposphere.
options.C: decrease in thickness of ozone layer in the stratosphere.
options.D: increase in the thickness of ozone layer in the troposphere.
options.E: increase in the thickness of ozone layer in the stratosphere.

explanation_steps: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere (about 15–35 km up). The ‘ozone hole’ is not a real hole but a severe seasonal thinning of this layer, mainly over Antarctica, caused by CFCs.
So the best description is a decrease in the thickness of the ozone layer in the stratosphere. Answer: C.
tips: Beware of the literal option ‘a hole’ – scientists use the word for thinning (below 220 Dobson units).

similar_questions.stem: Which substances are mainly blamed for destroying stratospheric ozone?
explanation_steps: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that break down ozone; the Montreal Protocol (1987) bans them. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA Ozone Watch; UNEP Ozone Secretariat – ‘What is the ozone hole?’

questions.stem: To which country does the present UN Secretary-General belong?
explanation_steps: The UN Secretary-General since 1 January 2017 is António Guterres, a former Prime Minister of Portugal.
Portugal is not among the options: Kofi Annan was from Ghana, Ban Ki-moon from South Korea, Dag Hammarskjöld from Sweden.
The item seems to confuse Portugal with its Iberian neighbour Spain, so C is the setter's most likely key – but strictly no option is correct.
tips: Secretaries-General to remember: Hammarskjöld (Sweden), U Thant (Burma), Boutros-Ghali (Egypt), Annan (Ghana), Ban (South Korea), Guterres (Portugal, 2017– ).

similar_questions.stem: Which African served as UN Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006?
explanation_steps: Kofi Annan of Ghana (1997–2006) won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: United Nations – Secretary-General biography (António Guterres)
textbook_ref.note: Guterres was re-appointed for 2022–2026; a new Secretary-General takes office in January 2027.

questions.review_flag: No correct option: Guterres is Portuguese and Portugal is not offered. Keyed C (Spain) as the probable intended answer; teacher may void or accept none.

questions.stem: Which of the following commodity groups dominate shipping trade?
explanation_steps: By tonnage, the largest share of world seaborne trade is energy: crude oil, oil products, liquefied gas and coal together make up roughly 40% of all cargo carried by sea (UNCTAD).
Grain, ores and containerised manufactures are carried in large amounts too, but fuel and energy is the biggest single group. Answer: C.
tips: Tankers (oil and gas) and bulk carriers (coal, ore, grain) carry most sea cargo by weight; container ships carry most by value.

similar_questions.stem: Which type of ship carries crude oil across the oceans?
explanation_steps: Crude oil and oil products travel in tankers. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: UNCTAD – Review of Maritime Transport 2018 (seaborne trade by cargo type)

questions.review_flag: Depends on the measure: by weight energy cargo (oil, gas, coal) leads; by value manufactured goods lead. Keyed C.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is known as ‘Economic Power House of Europe’?
explanation_steps: Germany has the largest economy in Europe (4th in the world by GDP) and is a leading exporter of cars, machinery and chemicals.
It is therefore often called the economic powerhouse (engine) of Europe. Answer: D.
tips: Largest European economies: Germany > UK > France > Italy.

similar_questions.stem: Which country has the largest economy in the European Union?
explanation_steps: Germany's GDP is the largest in the EU. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: IMF World Economic Outlook database; Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Germany (economy)

questions.stem: Which musical instrument is reputed to be the oldest in the world?
explanation_steps: Percussion (drums) is thought to be among humanity's oldest instruments – striking objects and skins goes back to prehistoric times.
The guitar, piano (c. 1700) and saxophone (1840s) are recent; jazz is a style of music, not an instrument. Answer: C.
tips: Eliminate the non-instrument (jazz) and the modern inventions.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a style of music rather than an instrument?
explanation_steps: Reggae is a musical style from Jamaica; the others are instruments. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Percussion instrument; Musical instrument (prehistory)

questions.review_flag: Archaeologically the oldest surviving instruments are bone flutes (c. 40,000 years); among the options the drum is the intended answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following media is different from the others?
explanation_steps: CNN, BBC, Al Jazeera and ERi-TV are news broadcasters (television/radio stations).
Google is an internet search engine/technology company, not a broadcaster. Answer: C.
tips: Odd-one-out: find the common category of four and the one that falls outside it.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Dimtsi Hafash is a radio station; the others are internet social-media/messaging platforms. Answer: D.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Google; broadcasting

questions.stem: How many women have currently ministerial positions in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: In 2019 four ministries were headed by women: Justice (Fozia Hashim), Health (Amna Nurhusein), Tourism (Askalu Menkerios) and Labour and Human Welfare (Luul Gebreab).
The paper prints the options as A 2, B 3, E 4, D 1, E 5; the third option (4) is stored here as C. Answer: C (4).
tips: Local civics facts change – check the current cabinet list on shabait.com before the exam.

similar_questions.stem: Which Eritrean ministry has been headed by Fozia Hashim since independence?
explanation_steps: Fozia Hashim has been Minister of Justice since 1993. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: CIA World Leaders – Eritrea; Martin Plaut (2024) list of long-serving Eritrean ministers
textbook_ref.note: Time-sensitive: four women ministers in 2019; in January 2026 Dr Halima Mohammed was appointed Minister of Education, so the number has changed.

questions.review_flag: Misprinted option letters (A, B, E, D, E): the answer ‘4’ is the third option, stored as C. Cabinet counts are time-sensitive; teacher to confirm.

questions.stem: Who suggested the theory of evolution through the process of natural selection?
explanation_steps: Charles Darwin (with Alfred Russel Wallace) proposed evolution by natural selection; Darwin's ‘On the Origin of Species’ appeared in 1859.
Einstein – relativity; Edison – electric light bulb; Franklin – electricity/lightning; Newton – gravity and laws of motion. Answer: A.
tips: Match scientists to their big idea.

similar_questions.stem: Who formulated the three laws of motion?
explanation_steps: Isaac Newton published the laws of motion in 1687. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Charles Darwin

questions.stem: Which of the following food staffs is the best source of protein?
explanation_steps: Fish contains about 20 g of protein per 100 g; milk about 3.4 g, bread about 8–9 g, lettuce about 1 g, and butter is almost all fat.
Answer: B.
tips: Body-building (protein) foods: meat, fish, eggs, beans, lentils; energy foods: bread, butter; protective foods: vegetables.

similar_questions.stem: Which food is richest in carbohydrates?
explanation_steps: Injera (teff) is mainly starch – a carbohydrate food. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: USDA FoodData Central (protein content of foods); WHO healthy diet

questions.stem: Which of the following statements advertises against smoking cigarette?

options.B: The price of cigarette is cheap.
options.D: Smoking cigarette is bad for health.

explanation_steps: An anti-smoking message warns people of the harm of smoking.
Both ‘causes cancer’ (C) and ‘is bad for health’ (D) do this; A and B would encourage smoking. Answer: E.
tips: If two options are both correct and a ‘C and D’ option exists, choose the combined option.

similar_questions.stem: Which slogan promotes hand-washing?
explanation_steps: Only B gives a reason to wash hands. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Tobacco fact sheet

questions.stem: Coluli mining exploration in the Southern Red Sea Zone is associated with one of the following minerals.
explanation_steps: The Colluli project in the Danakil depression (Southern Red Sea zone) is a large potash (sulphate of potash fertiliser) deposit, developed by the Colluli Mining Share Company (ENAMCO with Danakali/later partners).
Gold, copper and zinc are mined at Bisha and Zara (Gash-Barka/Anseba). Answer: D.
tips: Eritrean mines: Bisha (gold, copper, zinc), Zara/Koka (gold), Asheli (copper-gold), Colluli (potash).

similar_questions.stem: The Bisha mine in Gash-Barka mainly produces
explanation_steps: Bisha started as a gold mine (2011) and then produced copper and zinc concentrates. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Danakali Ltd – Colluli Potash Project; Eritrea Ministry of Energy and Mines

questions.stem: The full form of ‘WWW’ is?
explanation_steps: WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked web pages invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989–91 and accessed over the internet.
Answer: C.
tips: The web is not the internet: the internet is the network; the web is one service that runs on it.

similar_questions.stem: Who invented the World Wide Web?
explanation_steps: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web at CERN (1989). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: CERN – The birth of the Web

questions.stem: The most northern tip of Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Ras Kasar (Ras Kassar), a cape on the Red Sea at the Sudan border (about 18°N), is Eritrea's northernmost point.
Karora is the northernmost town (inland, slightly south); Ras Dumeira is the south-eastern tip at the Djibouti border; Dadda'to is in the far south-east; Alghena is a town in the north. Answer: B.
tips: Eritrea's extreme points: north – Ras Kasar; south-east – Ras Dumeira; west – near Om Hajer on the Setit.

similar_questions.stem: Ras Dumeira, disputed with Djibouti in 2008, lies at Eritrea's
explanation_steps: Ras Dumeira is at the south-eastern end of the Eritrean coast, at the Djibouti border. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) / Wikipedia – Ras Kasar (northernmost point of Eritrea, 18°00′N)

questions.review_flag: Karora (A) is the northernmost town and may be what some candidates chose; the northernmost point is the cape Ras Kasar (B).

questions.stem: One of the following statements <u>is not</u> true.

options.A: Canada is the second largest country in the world by area.
options.B: China is the first largest country by population.
options.C: Russia is the first largest country by area.
options.D: India is the second largest country by area.
options.E: The USA is the first largest country by economy.

explanation_steps: By area: 1 Russia, 2 Canada, 3 USA/China, … India is 7th. So D is false.
In 2019 China had the largest population and the USA the largest economy (nominal GDP) – both true then. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following pollutants has long lasting effect on the environment?
explanation_steps: Many pesticides (e.g. DDT and other organochlorines) are persistent organic pollutants: they break down very slowly, stay in soil and water for years and accumulate along food chains.

tips: Persistent + bio-accumulating = long-lasting (DDT, Stockholm Convention).
